rules.question: When is the Q3 2026 Form 941 due?
rules.whyItMatters: Sets the filing deadline. A due date on a weekend moves to the next business day, and deposits made on time and in full allow filing until the 10th day of the second month after the quarter.
rules.effective: Instructions for Form 941 (Rev. March 2026), which the IRS expects to be used for the second, third and fourth quarters of 2026.
rules.excerpt: Your Form 941 is due by the last day of the month that follows the end of the quarter. ... 3. July, August, September September 30 October 31 ... If you made timely deposits in full payment of your taxes for the quarter, you may file by the 10th day of the 2nd month that follows the end of the quarter. ... If any due date for filing falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday, you may file your return on the next business day.
matchPhrases: your form 941 is due by the last day of the month that follows the end of the quarter
3. july, august, september september 30 october 31
if you made timely deposits in full payment of your taxes for the quarter, you may file by the 10th day of the 2nd month that follows the end of the quarter
if any due date for filing falls on a saturday, sunday, or legal holiday, you may file your return on the next business day
at this time, the irs expects the march 2026 revision of form 941 and these instructions to also be used for the second, third, and fourth quarters of 2026
rules.pageOrSection: When to file (due dates table and the weekend rule); Reminders
rules.ruleOrLimit: The third-quarter return is due October 31. A due date on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday moves to the next business day. With timely deposits in full payment of the quarter's taxes, the return may be filed by the 10th day of the second month after the quarter.
rules.hangsApplication: October 31, 2026 is a Saturday, so the Q3 return is due Monday, November 2, 2026. The deposit log shows all six Q3 deposits made on the due dates for the full payday liabilities, $690,018.44 in all, equal to line 12, so the return may be filed by Tuesday, November 10, 2026. When these rules were written on November 5, 2026, November 2 had passed and November 10 had not. If LABOR-01 is decided as employment, the deposits were not in full payment and the November 10 date would not be available.
hangsFactsUsed: Q3 2026 federal tax deposits (dates and amounts)
rules.unresolved: Unsigned draft. A person reviews, signs and files the return (RETURN-01); nothing has been filed.

rules.question: Which employees are counted on line 1, and what goes on lines 2 and 3?
rules.whyItMatters: Line 1 counts only the payroll for the pay period that includes September 12. Line 2 must agree with box 1 of the Forms W-2, and line 3 is the income tax actually withheld.
rules.excerpt: Enter the number of employees on your payroll for the pay period including March 12, June 12, September 12, or December 12, for the quarter indicated at the top of Form 941. ... Enter amounts on line 2 that would also be included in box 1 of your employees’ Forms W-2. ... Enter the federal income tax you withheld (or were required to withhold) from your employees on this quarter’s wages, tips, taxable fringe benefits, and supplemental unemployment compensation benefits.
matchPhrases: enter the number of employees on your payroll for the pay period including march 12, june 12, september 12, or december 12, for the quarter indicated at the top of form 941
enter amounts on line 2 that would also be included in box 1 of your employees' forms w-2

enter the federal income tax you withheld (or were required to withhold) from your employees on this quarter's wages, tips, taxable fringe benefits, and supplemental unemployment compensation benefits
employers must use an employee's updated form w-4, if one is submitted by the employee, and the federal income tax withholding procedures in pub. 15-t
overtime compensation is still generally subject to both the employer share and employee share of social security tax and medicare tax
rules.pageOrSection: Part 1, lines 1, 2 and 3; What's New, withholding on qualified overtime compensation
rules.ruleOrLimit: Line 1 is the number of employees on the payroll for the pay period that includes September 12. Line 2 is the quarter's wages that belong in box 1 of the Forms W-2. Line 3 is the federal income tax withheld, or required to be withheld, from the quarter's wages; withholding follows each employee's Form W-4 and the Pub. 15-T procedures. The 2026 deduction for qualified overtime is claimed on employees' own returns, and overtime pay stays subject to both shares of Social Security and Medicare tax.
rules.hangsApplication: Line 1: the pay period including Saturday, September 12, 2026 ran from Monday, August 31 to Sunday, September 13 and was paid Friday, September 18 to 93 employees, so line 1 is 93. Ninety-six employees were paid during the quarter; the three employees leaving on July 17, August 14 and August 27 were not on that payroll. Line 2: gross pay on the six Q3 paydays, $2,681,087.98, less 401(k) deferrals of $95,016.10 and Section 125 health premiums of $49,356.00, is $2,536,715.88, the register's federal income tax wages. Line 3: $302,814.77, the federal income tax the payroll system withheld, taken from the register as calculated. The machine does not recompute income tax withholding.

rules.question: How do 401(k) deferrals and Section 125 premiums change income tax, Social Security and Medicare wages?
rules.whyItMatters: 401(k) deferrals come out of income tax wages but stay in Social Security and Medicare wages; Section 125 health premiums come out of all three. Mixing the two up would misstate lines 2, 5a and 5c.
rules.excerpt: Elective employee contributions and deferrals to a plan containing a qualified cash or deferred compensation arrangement (401(k)). Generally exempt, but see section 402(g) for limitation. Taxable. Taxable. ... Cafeteria plan benefits under section 125. If employee chooses cash or other taxable benefit, subject to all employment taxes. If employee chooses a nontaxable benefit, the treatment is the same as if the benefit was provided outside the plan.
matchPhrases: elective employee contributions and deferrals to a plan containing a qualified cash or deferred compensation arrangement (401(k)). generally exempt, but see section 402(g) for limitation. taxable. taxable.

cafeteria plan benefits under section 125. if employee chooses cash or other taxable benefit, subject to all employment taxes. if employee chooses a nontaxable benefit, the treatment is the same as if the benefit was provided outside the plan
rules.pageOrSection: Section 15, Special Rules for Various Types of Services and Payments (retirement and pension plans; cafeteria plan benefits)
rules.ruleOrLimit: Elective 401(k) deferrals are generally exempt from income tax withholding (within the section 402(g) limit) but taxable for Social Security, Medicare and FUTA. A nontaxable benefit chosen under a section 125 cafeteria plan is treated as if provided outside the plan.
rules.hangsApplication: In Q3 the payroll register shows $95,016.10 of 401(k) elective deferrals and $49,356.00 of Section 125 health premiums. The deferrals stay in Social Security and Medicare wages and the premiums come out of all three: line 2 is $2,681,087.98 less $95,016.10 and $49,356.00, or $2,536,715.88; Medicare wages on line 5c are $2,681,087.98 less $49,356.00, or $2,631,731.98.

rules.question: Are the Section 125 health premiums left out of Social Security and Medicare wages as well as income tax wages?
rules.whyItMatters: Health coverage paid through a cafeteria plan is a qualified benefit, exempt from all three, which is why Medicare wages on line 5c are less than gross pay.
rules.excerpt: A cafeteria plan, including an FSA, provides participants an opportunity to receive qualified benefits on a pre-tax basis. ... Accident and health benefits (but not Archer medical savings accounts (Archer MSAs) or long-term care insurance). ... Accident and health benefits Exempt (except 2% shareholder-employees of S corporations). Exempt Exempt
matchPhrases: a cafeteria plan, including an fsa, provides participants an opportunity to receive qualified benefits on a pre-tax basis
accident and health benefits (but not archer medical savings accounts (archer msas) or long-term care insurance)

rules.ruleOrLimit: Accident and health benefits are qualified cafeteria plan benefits, exempt from income tax withholding (except for 2% shareholder-employees of S corporations), and exempt from Social Security, Medicare and FUTA.
rules.hangsApplication: HANGS General Contracting LP is a partnership, so the S corporation exception does not arise. The register's Section 125 health premiums, $49,356.00 in Q3, are excluded from income tax wages (line 2, $2,536,715.88), Social Security wages (line 5a, $2,498,827.60) and Medicare wages (line 5c, $2,631,731.98) on every paycheck.

rules.question: Which wages go on line 5a, and where does Social Security stop for each employee?
rules.whyItMatters: Social Security tax stops once an employee's wages for the year reach $184,500. Two employees passed that base, so line 5a is lower than the Medicare wages on line 5c.
rules.excerpt: The social security tax rate is 6.2% each for the employee and employer. The social security wage base limit is $184,500. ... For 2026, the rate of social security tax on taxable wages is 6.2% (0.062) each for the employer and employee. Stop paying social security tax on and entering an employee’s wages on line 5a when the employee’s taxable wages and tips reach $184,500 for the year. ... line 5a (column 1) x 0.124 line 5a (column 2)

stop paying social security tax on and entering an employee's wages on line 5a when the employee's taxable wages and tips reach $184,500 for the year
line 5a (column 1) x 0.124 line 5a (column 2)
rules.ruleOrLimit: Social Security tax is 6.2% each for employee and employer on wages up to $184,500 for 2026. An employee's wages leave line 5a once the year's taxable wages reach $184,500; column 2 is column 1 times 0.124.
rules.hangsApplication: Each paycheck's Social Security wages are gross pay less Section 125 premiums, capped at $184,500 for the year using the year-to-date file. Alicia Abernathy (E-1001), Managing Director, had $184,500.00 of Social Security wages through June 30, the full base, so none of the Q3 pay is on line 5a. Andre Halvorsen (E-1002), Director of Operations, had $155,000.04 through June and reached the base on the August 7 payday ($5,653.80 of $11,923.08 that day): Q3 Social Security wages $29,499.96. Line 5a column 1 $2,498,827.60 x 0.124 = $309,854.62.

rules.question: What is the Social Security Administration's contribution and benefit base for 2026?
rules.whyItMatters: The base is the most wages subject to Social Security tax for each employee in a year; the Form 941 instructions and the payroll system must use the same figure.
rules.effective: Social Security Administration notice dated October 30, 2025, published November 3, 2025 (90 FR 49047), for remuneration paid in 2026.
rules.excerpt: Cost-of-Living Increase and Other Determinations for 2026 ... The OASDI contribution and benefit base is $184,500 for remuneration paid in 2026 and self-employment income earned in tax years beginning in 2026. The OASDI contribution and benefit base serves as the maximum annual earnings on which OASDI taxes are paid.

rules.pageOrSection: OASDI Contribution and Benefit Base (90 FR 49047 to 49053)
rules.ruleOrLimit: For 2026 the OASDI contribution and benefit base is $184,500: the most wages on which Social Security tax is paid for each employee in 2026.
rules.hangsApplication: The payroll system caps 2026 Social Security wages at $184,500, the same base the Form 941 instructions use: Alicia Abernathy (E-1001) had reached it by June 30 and Andre Halvorsen (E-1002) reached it on the August 7 payday. rules.question: Which wages go on lines 5c and 5d, and at what multipliers?
rules.whyItMatters: Medicare has no wage limit. Additional Medicare applies only to each employee's wages over $200,000 for the year and has no employer share, so line 5d uses 0.009, not 0.029.
rules.excerpt: Unlike social security wages, there is no limit on the amount of wages subject to Medicare tax. The rate of Medicare tax is 1.45% (0.0145) each for the employer and employee. ... line 5c (column 1) x 0.029 line 5c (column 2) ... Enter all wages, tips, sick pay, and taxable fringe benefits that are subject to Additional Medicare Tax withholding. ... Additional Medicare Tax is only imposed on the employee. There is no employer share of Additional Medicare Tax. ... line 5d (column 1) x 0.009 line 5d (column 2)

unlike social security wages, there is no limit on the amount of wages subject to medicare tax. the rate of medicare tax is 1.45% (0.0145) each for the employer and employee
line 5c (column 1) x 0.029 line 5c (column 2)

rules.ruleOrLimit: Line 5c is all Medicare wages, with no limit, times 0.029 (1.45% each for employee and employer). Line 5d is the wages subject to Additional Medicare Tax withholding times 0.009; there is no employer share.
rules.hangsApplication: Medicare wages are gross pay less Section 125 premiums on every paycheck, with no cap: line 5c $2,631,731.98 x 0.029 = $76,320.23. Line 5d $114,280.41 x 0.009 = $1,028.52.

rules.question: When must Additional Medicare Tax be withheld from a paycheck?
rules.whyItMatters: Withholding starts in the pay period in which the year's wages from this employer pass $200,000 and continues through December; starting early or late would misstate line 5d and the paychecks.
rules.excerpt: In addition to withholding Medicare tax at 1.45%, you must withhold a 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax from wages you pay to an employee in excess of $200,000 in a calendar year. You’re required to begin withholding Additional Medicare Tax in the pay period in which you pay wages in excess of $200,000 to an employee and continue to withhold it each pay period until the end of the calendar year.

rules.pageOrSection: Section 9, Withholding From Employees' Wages (Additional Medicare Tax withholding)
rules.ruleOrLimit: Withhold 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax on wages paid to an employee over $200,000 in the calendar year, starting in the pay period in which $200,000 is passed and continuing to the end of the year.

Andre Halvorsen's passed $200,000 on the August 21 payday: 0.9% of $2,692.36, $24.23, then $107.31 on September 4 and on September 18. Additional Medicare withheld in Q3: $1,028.53 on $114,280.41 of wages.

rules.question: Does a married filing status change when Additional Medicare withholding starts?
rules.whyItMatters: Withholding turns on the wages this employer pays, not on the employee's filing status, other income or a spouse's wages.
rules.effective: 26 CFR 31.3102-4 as published in the eCFR, text from Cornell Law School's Legal Information Institute.
rules.excerpt: An employer is required to collect from each of its employees the tax imposed by section 3101(b)(2) (Additional Medicare Tax) with respect to wages for employment performed for the employer by the employee only to the extent the employer pays wages to the employee in excess of $200,000 in a calendar year. This rule applies regardless of the employee's filing status or other income.

rules.question: Why does line 7 show a $0.30 adjustment?
rules.whyItMatters: Line 5 applies the statutory rates to the quarter's totals, while payroll rounds the tax on each paycheck; line 7 brings the return to the employee tax actually withheld.
rules.excerpt: Enter adjustments for fractions of cents (due to rounding) relating to the employee share of social security and Medicare taxes withheld. The employee share of amounts shown in column 2 of lines 5a–5d may differ slightly from amounts actually withheld from employees’ pay due to the rounding of social security and Medicare taxes based on statutory rates. This adjustment may be a positive or a negative adjustment.

rules.question: Which box is checked on line 16, and must Schedule B be attached?
rules.whyItMatters: A semiweekly schedule depositor reports each payday's liability on Schedule B instead of monthly totals on line 16; reporting the wrong way can bring an averaged deposit penalty.

rules.excerpt: For 2026, the lookback period begins July 1, 2024, and ends June 30, 2025. ... If you reported more than $50,000 of taxes for the lookback period, you’re a semiweekly schedule depositor. Check the third box on line 16. You must complete Schedule B (Form 941) and submit it with your Form 941. ... If you’re a monthly schedule depositor and accumulate a $100,000 tax liability on any day during the deposit period, you become a semiweekly schedule depositor on the next day and remain so for at least the rest of the calendar year and for the following calendar year.

rules.question: What goes on Schedule B, and what must it equal?
rules.whyItMatters: The IRS uses Schedule B to test whether each deposit was on time, so each liability belongs on the day wages were paid, and the quarter's total must equal line 12.
rules.effective: Instructions for Schedule B (Form 941) (Rev. June 2025), the revision the IRS publishes for 2026 returns.
rules.excerpt: File Schedule B if you’re a semiweekly schedule depositor. You’re a semiweekly schedule depositor if you reported more than $50,000 of employment taxes in the lookback period or accumulated a tax liability of $100,000 or more on any given day in the current or prior calendar year. ... On Schedule B, list your tax liability for each day. Your tax liability is based on the dates wages were paid. ... Your total liability for the quarter must equal line 12 on Form 941.
matchPhrases: file schedule b if you're a semiweekly schedule depositor
accumulated a tax liability of $100,000 or more on any given day in the current or prior calendar year
on schedule b, list your tax liability for each day. your tax liability is based on the dates wages were paid
enter your tax liabilities in the spaces that correspond to the dates you paid wages to your employees, not the date payroll liabilities were accrued or deposits were made
your total liability for the quarter must equal line 12 on form 941
rules.pageOrSection: Filing requirement; tax liability by month; total liability for the quarter
rules.ruleOrLimit: A semiweekly schedule depositor files Schedule B, listing each day's liability (income tax withheld plus both shares of Social Security and Medicare tax) on the date wages were paid, not when accrued or deposited; the quarter's total must equal Form 941 line 12.
rules.hangsApplication: Schedule B lists the six Q3 paydays: July 10 $106,871.15 and July 24 $119,961.81 (month 1, $226,832.96); August 7 $119,969.44 and August 21 $120,560.36 (month 2, $240,529.80); September 4 $118,621.12 and September 18 $104,034.56 (month 3, $222,655.68). The total, $690,018.44, equals line 12. Each day's liability is that payday's income tax withheld plus the employee and employer Social Security and Medicare tax, and the employee's Additional Medicare.

rules.question: When was each Q3 deposit due?
rules.whyItMatters: A payday carrying $100,000 or more of tax must be deposited by the next business day instead of the semiweekly date, and a weekend or a District of Columbia legal holiday moves that day.
rules.excerpt: If you accumulate $100,000 or more in taxes on any day during a monthly or semiweekly deposit period ..., you must deposit the tax by the next business day, whether you’re a monthly or semiweekly schedule depositor. ... A business day is any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday. ... The term “legal holiday” means any legal holiday in the District of Columbia. ... July 3—Independence Day (observed) September 7—Labor Day

rules.pageOrSection: Section 11, Depositing Taxes (semiweekly deposit schedule; $100,000 Next-Day Deposit Rule; Deposits Due on Business Days Only; legal holidays for 2026)
rules.ruleOrLimit: Semiweekly: Wednesday to Friday paydays are due the following Wednesday. Taxes of $100,000 or more accumulated on any day are due the next business day. Business days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and District of Columbia legal holidays, which in Q3 2026 are July 3 and September 7. Deposits follow the dates wages are paid, not accruals.
rules.hangsApplication: All six Q3 paydays were Fridays, so under the semiweekly schedule each deposit would be due the following Wednesday. Each payday's taxes were $100,000 or more ($104,034.56 to $120,560.36), so each deposit was due the next business day instead: July 13, July 27, August 10, August 24, September 8 and September 21. The September 4 deposit was due Tuesday, September 8, because September 7 was Labor Day; July 3 moved no Q3 deposit. The deposits follow the paydays, not the ledger's June 30 and September 30 wage accruals.

rules.question: Were the Q3 deposits on time and in full, and what would a late deposit cost?
rules.whyItMatters: A deposit must cover 100% of the liability by its due date; small shortfalls are excused only under the accuracy rule, and late deposits carry penalties of 2% to 15%.
rules.excerpt: You’re required to deposit 100% of your tax liability on or before the deposit due date. However, penalties won’t be applied for depositing less than 100% if both of the following conditions are met. Any deposit shortfall doesn’t exceed the greater of $100 or 2% of the amount of taxes otherwise required to be deposited. ... 2% Deposits made 1 to 5 days late. 5% Deposits made 6 to 15 days late. 10% Deposits made 16 or more days late, but before 10 days from the date of the first notice the IRS sent asking for the tax due.

rules.pageOrSection: Section 11, Accuracy of Deposits Rule; Deposit Penalties
rules.ruleOrLimit: Deposit 100% of each liability by its due date. A shortfall of no more than the greater of $100 or 2% is excused if made up by the makeup date. Late deposits cost 2% (1 to 5 days), 5% (6 to 15 days), 10% (16 days or more, before 10 days after the first IRS notice) and 15% (unpaid more than 10 days after that notice), counted in calendar days from the due date.

rules.question: Is Tomas Arvelo, paid by the hour through accounts payable, an employee for Form 941?
rules.whyItMatters: An employee's wages carry income tax withholding and both shares of Social Security and Medicare tax; payments to an independent contractor carry neither. Treating an employee as a contractor without a reasonable basis can make the business liable for the employment taxes.
rules.effective: The IRS page, saved copy retrieved November 5, 2026.
rules.excerpt: In determining whether the person providing service is an employee or an independent contractor, all information that provides evidence of the degree of control and independence must be considered. ... The keys are to look at the entire relationship and consider the extent of the right to direct and control the worker. ... If you classify an employee as an independent contractor and you have no reasonable basis for doing so, then you may be held liable for employment taxes for that worker
matchPhrases: it is critical that business owners correctly determine whether the individuals providing services are employees or independent contractors

the keys are to look at the entire relationship and consider the extent of the right to direct and control the worker
if you classify an employee as an independent contractor and you have no reasonable basis for doing so, then you may be held liable for employment taxes for that worker
you may consider submitting a form ss-8, determination of worker status for purposes of federal employment taxes and income tax withholding
rules.pageOrSection: Determining whether the individuals providing services are employees or independent contractors; Common law rules; Form SS-8; Misclassification of employees
rules.ruleOrLimit: Worker status follows the common-law rules: behavioral control, financial control and the type of relationship, weighed together with no single deciding factor. Form SS-8 asks the IRS to decide.
rules.hangsApplication: Tomas Arvelo, an individual, was paid $21,168.00 through accounts payable in Q3 for 504 hours of concrete finishing at $42.00 an hour, in 13 weekly payments from July 2 to September 25, working under the HGC foreman at Tideflats Cold Storage. The vendor list shows a Form W-9 with a Social Security number and no contractor registration, UBI or certificate of insurance on file. The draft reports the payroll as recorded and adds nothing for this work.
rules.unresolved: Reason: worker status turns on the whole relationship, and the files show only the payments, the hours and the supervision note. Whether Tomas Arvelo is an employee is a common-law question for a person (LABOR-01); treating the work as employment would change lines 2, 3 and 5 and the deposits.
